dialogue.describe: I'm… short… of breath…
dialogue.offer: I'm asthmatic.  I need you to get some kind of medicinal tea for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without your help!
dialogue.advice: I'm dead unless I can get this special tea.  Maybe it's from a flower?
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: This infection is bad, <very> bad…
dialogue.offer: I'm infected.  Badly.  I need you to get something antiseptic for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry.  Get me some cattail jelly.  That should hopefully be good enough.
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without your help!
dialogue.advice: I think if you can pull cattail jelly out of some cattails from like a swamp or something, I can smear it on the wound.
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: Does our flag still yet wave?  Maybe we will have to make it.
dialogue.offer: You haven't truly visited a place until you've driven a flagpole down into its dirt.  I've got the pole and the paint here, but I need a large canvas for the flag itself.  Get me a large sheet woven out of grass, and we can claim this land in the name of America!
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya!  Fetch me a large grass sheet!  Large enough to be used as a blanket!
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  God damned commie…
dialogue.advice: You'll need to collect some straw and spin it into yarn first.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!  I name this land…  New New England!  How does that sound?  I like it!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: You give up?  Our country fell apart because no one could find a good man to rely on, and now you're telling me this place ain't any better?  Might as well give up, I guess.

dialogue.describe: Those twisted snakes…
dialogue.offer: I left my dream journal in the swamp while I was doing my naked snake yoga.  There's some pretty wild stuff in there so I want it back.
dialogue.accepted: Please don't read it unless you are prepared for some graphic and disturbing content.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but I want it.  I have an incredible imagination.  I had a dream about a horse once and it talked.  Amazing stuff.
dialogue.advice: The swamps are pretty dangerous and I'm not really sure where I was.  If you want to just make me a new dream journal that would be all right too.
dialogue.success: Great, let's see…  Oh.  Well I can just start over I guess.  My imagination is an endless play place of amazement!
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: Now my nightmares are let loose upon the shivering land.

name.str: Find Patient Records in Leather Journal

dialogue.describe: I hope I don't see many names I know…
dialogue.offer: I've lost so many friends… please find me a patient list in a leather journal.  I just want to know who might still be out there.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, I suppose it won't change what has already happened but it will bring me closure.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just want to know what happened to everyone.
dialogue.advice: You may have some difficulties finding a full list with things how they are.  If you can't get me the list, can you just make or find me a leather journal for me to make my own?
dialogue.success: I'm making a list and checking it twice…
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

name.str: Find Weather Log in Leather Journal

dialogue.describe: I wonder if a retreat might exist…
dialogue.offer: Everyone who dies gets back up, right?  Which means that whatever is causing this it must be airborne to have infected everyone.  I believe that if that is the case then there should be regions that were not downwind from where-ever the disease was released.  We need to find a leather journal with all the weather patterns leading up to the outbreak.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks so much, you may save both of us yet.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: You may have some difficulties finding those weather pattern records with things how they are.  If you can't get me the list, can you just make or find me a leather journal for me to make my own?
dialogue.success: These look more complicated than I thought, just give me some time.
dialogue.success_lie: This isn't what we need.
dialogue.failure: If only we could find a great valley or something.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: As the world seems to abandon the reality that we once knew, it becomes plausible that the old superstitions that were cast aside may have had some truth to them.  Please go and find me a religious relic… I doubt it will be of much use but I've got to hope in something.  It will look like a normal rock to you, but I can divine secrets from its earthly essence.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I hear rocks may be found in the woods.  They tell me things.  The spirits.  Religion!
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a small relic.  Any relic will do.  It looks like a rock.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I need some time alone now…
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: I have learned so much from this sacred relic.  I have attuned to it.  We must go deeper.  I now understand that buried in the deep forest is a special place with even larger rocks, I mean sacred relics.  Go there, and get me a holy symbol of this place.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: The woods are deep and dark and probably dangerous.  Bring a friend if you can.
dialogue.success: Thank you, this is exactly what I was looking for.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: You have no idea how interesting this holy symbol is.  I have two very promising leads… first things first, I have learned of dark whispers of mystic significance, telluric resonances that tingle the spine and give me kind of a dizzy feeling, but not entirely unpleasant.  Could you investigate a location for me?  I'm not sure what was going on here but the whispers seem fairly worried about it.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… You may need it this time more than the past excursions you have gone on.  There is a whisper about potential human sacrifice in the days immediately before and after the grand mystical shift.  The name of the cult is not revealed to me, except for an incessant squeaking.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I doubt the site is still occupied but I'd carry some form of weapon at least… I'm not sure what you might be looking for but I'm positive you'll find something out of the ordinary if you look long enough.
dialogue.inquire: I'm positive there is something there… there has to be, any luck?
dialogue.success: Thank you, your account of these… demonic creations proves the fears the whispers had were well founded.  Our priority should be routing out any survivors of this cult… I don't known if they are responsible for the disaster but they certainly know more about it than I do.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: I have another task if you are feeling up to it.   There is a mad hermit that the whispers made special mention of.  I was wondering if you could see what may have happened to them or if they left anything behind.  The whispers admit the individual is rather unstable, to put it lightly, but the whispers believe the hermit was some kind of mystical visionary.  I'm not in a position to cast out the account just yet… it seems the hermit has prophesied events accurately before.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… I can only imagine that the island will be a little slice of hell.  I hope you can swim.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: With things as they are you probably won't just find a boat lying around.  Maybe make one?  Maybe swim?
dialogue.success: Thank you, I'm not sure what to make of this but I'll ponder your account.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I can't believe I forgot to bring it…
dialogue.offer: There's some important notes on my special stick that I need.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks!  Just get the stick and bring it to me.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Don't worry, you'll know the stick when you see it, it is unmistakable.
dialogue.inquire: So, do you have my stick yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent, thank you!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  All that work, down the drain…

dialogue.describe: You've seen these walking fungus things around?  I would like to take a closer look at their flesh.  For science.
dialogue.offer: I need someone to get a sample of strange alien fungus chunks and bring it to me.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent.  Get me those nasty chunks.
dialogue.rejected: Are you sure?  The scientific value of those smelly chunks could be priceless…
dialogue.advice: I was cutting up a fungus creature in a nearby forest.  I was chased of by a big raven before I could finish, but perhaps you are brave enough to fetch the remains.  Alternatively, you could go and kill and butcher one of those things yourself.
dialogue.inquire: Well, do you have the disgusting chunks yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent!  This may be the key to removing the infection.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, you couldn't possibly have the nasty chunks!  Liar!
dialogue.failure: What a shame, that horrible chunk could have proved invaluable…

dialogue.describe: The eater of the dead… something was ripping trees to shreds and only leaving a few scattered limbs…
dialogue.offer: A few days ago another survivor and I were in the woods.  One night something caught onto our trail and chased us for ten minutes or so until we decided to split up and meet-up back here.  My buddy never showed up and I don't have the means to kill whatever it was.  Can you lend a hand?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, make sure you're ready for whatever the beast is.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either.
dialogue.advice: Make sure you have a good weapon.  It sounded pretty big.
dialogue.success: You look a little shaken up, I can't tell you how glad I am that you killed it though.
dialogue.success_lie: Something in the shadows still seems to stare at me when I look at the woods.
dialogue.failure: I'm glad you came back alive… I wasn't sure if I had sent you to your death.

dialogue.describe: Oh god, I can't believe it happened…
dialogue.offer: My bear… she's… she was killed, but then she just got back up… she's one of those things now.  Can you put her out of her misery for me?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you… she would've wanted it this way.
dialogue.rejected: Please reconsider, I know she's suffering…
dialogue.advice: She's still a bear, and seemed furious, so be wary.  And please, make it quick…
dialogue.inquire: Well…?  Did you… finish things for my bear?
dialogue.success: Thank you.  I couldn't rest until I knew that was finished.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Really… that's too bad.

dialogue.describe: Oh, my poor puppy…
dialogue.offer: I left my stupid dog in the woods, not far from here.  Can you retrieve it?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you!  Please hurry back!
dialogue.rejected: Please, think of my poor little puppy!
dialogue.advice: Good luck!
dialogue.inquire: Have you found my dog yet?  His name is Sparky!
dialogue.success: Thank you so much for finding him!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Oh no!  My poor puppy…

name.str: Go into deep woods to retrieve family seeds

dialogue.describe: I need you to get my family seeds from the deep woods.
dialogue.offer: I left some special seeds from my family in the deep woods.  Can you get them?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, it's great to see someone willing to help out.
dialogue.rejected: Well, I'll find someone else to do it for me, maybe there are a lot of people left…
dialogue.advice: I'll know the seeds when I see them.  Just bring me any seeds you find.
dialogue.inquire: Got the seeds?  They're important to me.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  I'll be sure to put in a good word for you around the woods.  With like birds or whatever.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand it over.
dialogue.failure: Shit happens.

name.str: Gather cattail stalks to create cattail jelly

data.description: Gather <color_light_blue>80 cattail stalks</color> from the swamp and bring them back to <color_light_red>learn how to craft cattail jelly</color>.  Raise your <color_light_blue>survival skill to at least 1</color> by harvesting cattail stalks.  <color_light_blue>Bring back the provided bag</color> as well.

effect.u_message: You learn how to craft cattail jelly.

dialogue.describe: Medical services are a little sparse here, but people have been surviving using their wits and the bounty of Mother Nature for a long time.  Care to learn a little?
dialogue.offer: Did you know that cattails are a source of a jelly that works as an antiseptic and analgesic?  Something like that is likely to be mighty helpful out here.  I want you to take this bag, head to the nearest swamp, collect 80 cattail stalks, and bring them back here.  In exchange, I'll show you how to harvest the jelly.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  This bag should be big enough to hold all of the stalks we'll need.  Don't forget to bring it back.
dialogue.rejected: Your loss.
dialogue.advice: The cattails grow in the fresh water in swamps.  You can't miss them.
dialogue.inquire: Got those cattail stalks yet?  Don't forget to bring back my bag and to work on improving your survival skill as well.
dialogue.success: Great!  Hand them over and I'll show you how this works.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand them over.
dialogue.failure: Well, that's a shame.

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I want to <swear> burn it so bad…
dialogue.offer: I'm so <swear> infuriated!  I've got a tree that ruined my life, and now I want to get revenge!  I don't care about <the_cataclysm>, I just want to burn that tree!  Would you help me, <name_g>?
dialogue.accepted: Good.  Let's go to the tree and <swear> burn it down!  Oh, bring some tinder so we can start the fire.  I can make the sparks.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's such an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Maybe we can find a stick in the woods.
dialogue.success: Sweet, sweet revenge!  Ah, smells so nice!  Feels like the smell of napalm in the morning!  It will all burn to ashes in a matter of minutes.  You helped me get my revenge, so I'll follow you to the end, <name_g>!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  How…

data.dynamic_line: Are we there yet, <name_g>?  I can't wait to burn that tree!

data.description: Nobody around?  Oh well, it doesn't matter.  Your beloved goats are all you need!

data.name: Lost Tribal
data.description: You were out gathering for the tribe when the sky broke and the gods called to you, then you collapsed.  When you woke up, you were in an unfamiliar place with new memories crowding your thoughts.

data.name: Shaman
data.description: You've trained in the medical arts, refining natural remedies into real cures for disease.  Your tribe would have lived long and healthy lives, were they still here.

data.name: Backpacker
data.description: For the past few years you've been traveling the world, sightseeing and living off tribal donations.  You came home to find your home abandoned, and the only thing between you and death is the open fields and your pack.

data.name: Miner
data.description: You're a miner, not a minor!  Your waterskin is dry, you lost your haul, and you're on your last torch…

data.name: Bow Hunter
data.description: Ever since you were a child you loved hunting, and quickly developed a talent for archery.  Why, if the world ended, there's nothing you'd want at your side more than your trusty bow.  So, when it did, you made sure to bring it along.

data.name: Spear Hunter
data.description: Ever since you were a child you loved hunting, and quickly developed a talent for chasing down your prey with a spear.  Why, if the world ended, there's nothing you'd want at your side more than your trusty spear.  So, when it did, you made sure to bring it along.

data.name: Javelin Hunter
data.description: Ever since you were a child you loved hunting, and quickly developed a talent for javelin throwing.  Why, if the world ended, there's nothing you'd want at your side more than your trusty javelins.  So, when it did, you made sure to bring them along.

data.name: Crossbow Hunter
data.description: Ever since you were a child you loved hunting, and crossbow hunting was always your favorite.  Why, if the world ended, there's nothing you'd want at your side more than your trusty crossbow.  So, when it did, you made sure to bring it along, though most of your bolts were lost during the escape.

data.name: Fisher
data.description: You spent most of your days fishing in the swamp, getting by quietly on your catch.  You found the buzzing of insects enjoyable, but recently they've gotten bigger and meaner.  Now their horrible noises have you spooked - you just hope the fish aren't as nasty.
You spent most of your days fishing in lakes and swamps, getting by quietly on your catch.  While you've wandered from your canoe, you can't resist coming back for another catch.

data.name: Redsmith
data.description: You ran into trouble coming out from your forge, but despite the havoc you've managed to keep some of your equipment along with your latest project.

data.name: Survivor
data.description: Some would say that there's nothing particularly notable about you, but you've survived, and that's more than most could say right now.

data.name: Trapper
data.description: You spent most of your life trapping with your father.  Both of you made a decent living selling your catches and running trapping tutorials.  Hopefully, your skills will come in useful against less conventional game.

data.name: Tailor
data.description: Tailoring may not seem like the most useful skill when the world has ended.  Most people wouldn't expect a simple tailor to live very long.  This is your opportunity to prove them wrong.

data.name: Lumberjack
data.description: You're a lumberjack, and you're okay.  You felled trees before the world ended, and you suspect the undead aren't nearly as tough.

data.name: Musician
data.description: You nailed your solo, but the audience erupted into screams instead of applause.  You weren't able to grab much during the panic, but at least you have your flute in your basket.

data.name: Tribal Warrior Recruit
data.description: Joining the tribal guard has been your dream for years.  You finally got in, just in time for your training to get interrupted by some sort of emergency.  As far as you can tell, the elders abandoned you in this hellhole when you missed the emergency evac.
As a member of your tribe's elite guard, you sharpened your swordsmanship to the best that you could.  Now, you're a rōnin of the woods.

data.name: Tribal Arbalist
data.description: From your first hunt, you showed talent with a crossbow.  While the tribe was well guarded by your aim, you're all alone now.

data.name: Farmer
data.description: A patch of soil, some water, and sunlight were all you ever needed; why should things be any different now?  With a handful of seeds and your trusty hoe, it's time to rebuild the Earth, one plant at a time.

data.name: Native Settler
data.description: You were on the road with friends from your tribe to search for a new settlement spot when you seemed to be yanked somewhere completely different.  You see no sign of your friends, but at least you got your equipment and some seeds with you.

data.name: Carpenter
data.description: Living under your craftsmanship, the tribe was no longer bound to caves lest they freeze in the night.  You won't have to work nearly as hard for just yourself.

data.name: Bricklayer
data.description: Using the earth and organic material to create durable, insulated adobe kept your trade in high demand in your tribe.  Now alone, you only need to look out for yourself.

data.name: In a Cave
data.description: Somehow, you found yourself in a cave.  Someone else is with you.

data.name: A Lonely Cave
data.description: Somehow, you found yourself in a cave.  Seems like you're on your own.

data.name: Infected
data.description: In the chaos and panic of evacuation, you got bitten by something!  You didn't get proper medical care, and now the wound has started turning green.

data.name: Challenge - Hunted
data.description: Since the start of the Cataclysm, something has been hunting you relentlessly.  You can outrun it, but it always seems to find you eventually.  The only escape is for one of you to die.

data.name: Challenge - Fungal Infection
data.description: You feel spores crawling beneath your skin.  It's only a matter of time.

data.name: Challenge - Really Bad Day
data.description: You start drunk to the point of incapacitation, depressed, infected, surrounded by fire, and sick with the flu.  This day went downhill really fast.

data.name: Challenge - Bordered
data.description: You have survived the initial wave of panic, and have achieved (relative) safety in a wilderness.  The only thing that really bothers you is a mysterious sky-high wall seen in the distance.

data.name: Ambush
data.description: It is the winter after zero hour.  As you were scavenging for food and a warm place to stay at, you heard the sound of lots of movement nearby.

data.name: The Next Summer
data.description: A little over a year has passed since the apocalypse started, and you're about to face your second summer in Hell.

data.name: Last Flight
data.//: Doesn't seem to spawn the helicopter without a road nearby.  Disabled until this can be fixed.
data.description: Once it became clear that the world was ending you took to the skies, hoping that your flying skills could lead you to safety.  During your flight you got lost and had to land on an empty field.

data.name: Wilderness
data.description: You find yourself amongst trees.  The screaming and the moaning is fainter this far from civilization, but you'd better know what you're doing out here.

data.name: Car Crash
data.description: You decided the open road would be a better prospect than the zombie-filled cities.  While en route to your destination, you were involved in a wreck.  When you look around, you can no longer spot the road you were driving on.  Just how hard did you hit your head?
data.//: Came from a portal storm, so future tech/professions are allowed

data.name: Challenge - Portal Dependent
data.description: You were caught in a huge and unstable portal storm, and were utterly unprotected from the full force of its effects.  You're on the tail end of the storm now, and while you've survived, you feel… different.

data.name: Challenge - Medieval Peasant
data.description: Som nigromancie hath brought yow hidder!  Ye have only the hoose on youre legges and the knyf at youre syde and youre prayeres to Marie moder of God.
A battery for storing electrical power, and discharging it to power electrical devices built into the vehicle.  Contained in a clay shell.

info.name: Bionic Professions
info.description: Numerous bionic starting professions.

name.str: Free yourself from your bionic failures

data.description: You currently have some bionics malfunctioning.  Remove them and avoid any more faulty bionics in your body.

data.name: Bionic Athlete
data.description: You'll never get your shot at the Cyberolympics.  All that's left of your dream is a single leftover protein shake.  Well, that and your bulging, cybernetically-enhanced muscles.

data.name: Bionic Police Officer
data.description: Mortally injured in the line of duty, you were resurrected by the surgeons from the department's revolutionary Cybercop program.  Now, in these lawless times, you are truly the future of law enforcement.

data.name: Commercial Cyborg
data.description: You always had to have the latest and best gadgets and gizmos, so is it any wonder that you upgraded your flesh along with your smart phone?

data.name: Bionic Firefighter
data.description: As a second-generation augmented firefighter, you have been cybernetically enhanced to operate in the most dire of emergency situations.  You're pretty sure this counts.

data.name: Bionic Game Master
data.description: You came into a large fortune, through luck or will, and hosted games for world-famous celebrities.  You could afford to spoil your players, and so you did.  You invested in bionics to make you smarter and memorized the entire handbook.  Let's hope that knowledge helps you now.

data.name: Bionic Gangster
data.description: You were the boss's favorite, their protege; they always counted on you to get the toughest jobs done.  They invested in "basic" augments and the best gear on the market in preparation for your biggest hit yet.  Sadly, you came out of surgery to find your whole gang had been eaten.

data.name: Bionic Assassin
data.description: The product of millions of dollars of clandestine research, you are a bionic sleeper agent capable of silently engaging your target while maintaining an innocuous appearance.  Your handler cut all contact a week ago.

data.name: Augmentation Associate
data.description: When bionics first emerged, you were quick to make them into your career, and spent your days overseeing their installation.  That makes you one of the few non-zombies in the world that can calibrate an Autodoc, which might come in handy.

data.name: Bionic Surgeon
data.description: As one of the top surgeons in the country, you were chosen for an augmentation program to expand the medical field.  With your expertise and augmentations, you can perform precise surgery with little assistance.

data.name: Bionic Boffin
data.description: You were employed by a major international corporation as a representative and technical advisor, utilizing the incredible power of your cybernetically augmented mind.

data.name: Bionic Patient
data.description: When the diagnosis came back positive, you signed up for a series of experimental bionic surgeries that saved your life.  Now you're healthier than you ever were before, thanks to a suite of bionic systems powered by your own metabolic functions.  Make the most of your second chance at life.

data.name: Bionic Prepper
data.description: You knew the end was coming.  You augmented yourself with some basic bionic tools and underwent extensive survival training.  Now the end has come, and it is time to see if your efforts have paid off.

data.name: Bionic Runner
data.description: You were the kind of sportsman who couldn't get off the track.  You love running, and you enhanced your body with cybernetics to go even faster.  Now there's plenty to run from - this is your kind of game.

data.name: Bionic Sniper
data.description: A top-secret military program sought to convert you into the perfect sniper.  Your bionics, equipment, and extensive field training enable you to drop targets from implausible distances, even after weeks of total isolation in enemy territory.

data.name: Bionic Soldier
data.description: You are the result of one of the military's last research programs: a prototype cyborg soldier.  The wars they expected you to fight have become obsolete, but war never changes.

data.name: Bionic Agent
data.description: Your body conceals several bionic components, worth millions of dollars in public taxes.  The government turned you into an infiltration and recon specialist: you have night vision, an alarm, lock picking capabilities and a hacking module.

data.name: Bionic Student
data.description: Your parents were so obsessed with making sure you aced every test that they had you outfitted with bionics to enhance your intellect and memory.  Now you're facing the hardest test yet, and you're not sure if those are the right kind of tools for the job.

data.name: Bionic Thief
data.description: Impeccable style and a few bionic tricks up your sleeve have seen you pull off a string of daring, high-profile heists.  The cops would love to get their hands on you, but seem otherwise occupied.

data.name: Industrial Cyborg
data.description: For better or for worse, bionic augmentation has turned you into a walking power tool.  Upgraded with a standard industrial-grade manual labor surgery and training package, you are augmented with bionic muscles and an integrated toolset, both powered by standard batteries.

data.name: Prototype Cyborg
data.description: You were normal once.  Before the tests, before the procedures, before they stripped away every outward sign of your humanity.  You're more machine than human now, but that might prove to be an advantage against the horrors that await.

data.name: Cyberjunkie
data.description: Long ago your lifelong infatuation with bionic enhancement lead you into a shady world of back-alley bionic clinics and self-installed secondhand CBMs.  Your posthuman hunger still cries out to be fed; where will you get your bionic fix now?

data.name: Bionic Monster
data.description: Completely overtaken by bionic-induced psychosis, you are a deformed posthuman monster, forced to hide in the shadows.  Amidst the desolation, however, even a creature such as yourself might find its niche.

data.name: Failed Cyborg
data.description: After a series of surgical mistakes, your body is a wreck of bionic parts.  You have a large capacity for power, but are filled with broken and useless bionics.  Your ethanol power supply still works, at least.

data.name: Drone Operator
data.description: You had a job programming machines such as automatic street cleaners, newsbots, and pizza delivery drones.  Bionic implants helped you control them remotely.  Now all the drones carry guns instead of pizza.  At least you still have a… RC car?
Through a series of painful and expensive surgeries, you became a walking bionic weapon, your services as a mercenary available to the highest bidder.

data.name: High Tech, Low Life
data.description: Before the world ended, bionics were reserved for the rich and the famous.  You might not have been either, but you wanted in.  Hidden offices sequestered away in basements, anesthetic smuggled out of hospitals, and desperate people with little to lose could get you what you wanted.  If you went too deep, however, your augmentation may have come at a price…

data.dynamic_line:
Us call us the Exodii, eh?  An' other things, but that'n's good.  This're our home, such as it.  This'n's monicked as Rubik, and tassed with a trade an'.  You lookin' to trade?  Us'n's alay for the scrap, metal an' more as it be."

[TRANSLATE:] "We call ourselves the Exodii, eh?  And other things, but that's good.  This is our home, such as it is.  I'm called Rubik, and I've been assigned to trade with you.  Are you looking to trade?  We're always looking for scrap, metal and more.

dynamic_line: Good an' fine, then.
Have it as ye'll see.

For a card an' a wink, eh?"

[TRANSLATE:] "That was a good exchange.

data.dynamic_line:
That be a right welcher, eh?  Afore us'n were to this land, the preface were on a half-score century by the reckonin'.  Landed us in amidst of a war'd turned wrong, for an' as the dead had come back in.  By the butcher's block, not much an unusual case, really.  The enemy makes us fight.  By an' by, we came in, an' by then the killin' fields were plump and ready to harvest the bronze.  'Tain't no steel-of-the-lake, but 'tis a good dross metal for holdin' off a nibblin' mouth, so we kept a few o' their vestments an' stickers for to trade."

[TRANSLATE:] "It's a bit of a surprise, isn't it?  Before we came here, we were in a place about 600 years earlier in time, or so.  We landed in the middle of a war that turned wrong when the dead started joining back in.  Truth be told, not a very unusual situation.  The enemy makes us fight.  By and by, we came in, and by then the killing fields were ready for us to harvest their bronze.  It's no steel-of-the-lake, but it's a good strong metal for stopping a nibbling mouth, so we kept some of their armour and weapons to trade.

Ah, a real monger's eye, ye be.  Them's the mettle o' many a year of trials.  Us'n've been clashin wi' the enemy for a long an' then, an' o'er the turns us've worked out some vestments for the job.  Keep's a walker walkin' longer, an I'm ken.  This'n keeps some o' the parst in an' around, but ye'd be tassed to make the vestment with the grease o' your own brow."

[TRANSLATE:] "Ah, you've got a discerning eye.  They're the result of many years of work.  We've been fighting the enemy for a long time, and over the years we've worked out some armour for the job.  Keeps you going a bit longer in the field, if you ask me.  I keep some of the parts in stock, but you'll have to put it together yourself.

This 'n that, an I'm ken.  It be made for a fine wander, beladen with the goods o' the hunt, y'see.  By which I'm to say, 'tis well suited to carry all ye can wrest from the cold arms o' the deadlands, without troublin' your gait nor makin' it easy for the cold clutch o' the scrabblin' arm.  Be an' it is tough as a tarket's nut, I'd razz."

[TRANSLATE:] "This and that, you know.  It's made for a travelling scavenger, you see.  What I mean is, it's well suited to carry around whatever you pick up in the wastelands, without making it too hard to get around nor giving any easy handholds for scrambling arms.  That, and I'd say it's as tough as nails.

'Tis as simple as comes to a wobble.  Our vestment be oft made from the fine clothes and hides of the land, and our jibber tears the stuff o' life apart here and there when us'n travel.  For as some can be saved if care be taken, there be no case to store nigh enough o' this.  That, an' our manuc-makers run as hot as a sunstone, no spit'n taste for that which we don't use usselves."

[TRANSLATE:] "It's a simple matter of how we teleport.  Our clothes are often made from cloth and hides from wherever we visit, and our teleporter tears living stuff apart here and there when we travel.  Some can be saved if we take care, but there's no room to store nearly enough extra.  That, and our fabricators are always busy, no time to waste on stuff we don't need for ourselves

dynamic_line.yes:
Sure as you c'n try.  Us're not the greatest yarker, nor do it all for gratis, kennit."

[TRANSLATE:] "You can surely try.  I'm not the greatest speaker, and I won't just chat forever for free, you know.
dynamic_line.no:
Oy, c'n I bark you summat first?"

[TRANSLATE:] "Hey, can I ask you something first?

data.dynamic_line: 'Ow long's it been since the mess happened?
Thank ye.  When you an' Rubik first met, how long'd it been since the mess begun?

Lovely!  Benzete's gonna be a pair, that's a track!  I mean, they'll be right happy.  This is their first jump, and it's a flappin' duck."

[TRANSLATE:] "Lovely!  Benzete (this is a name) is going to be beside themselves, that's for sure.  I mean, they'll be really happy.  This is their first jump, and it's a lucky one.

So 'twere an I recalt, us're yarkin' of Benzete an' their great first jump."

[TRANSLATE:] "As I recall, we were talking about Benzete and how this is a great jump for their first time.

Us gotta leave the old world afore it's worn right to the gums, an y'ken, and find a nice twitchy one on t'other side.  Your deadland be a brand shiny"

[TRANSLATE:] "We've got to leave the old world before it gets too worn out, you see, and find a nice fresh one on the other side.  Your deadland is as fresh as it gets.

Neverken.  Right and so, the enemy is new here, and us'n have a few good hours in the sun beforenext the jump."

[TRANSLATE:] "No worries.  I mean, the enemy is new here, and we have a bit of safe time ahead of us before we have to jump away again.

That be a part an' switch, but this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that."

[TRANSLATE:] "That's a part of it, sure, but this is nice for other reasons, and much better than our last jump.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings are really useful to us.

You kennit rightly!  That and this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that."

[TRANSLATE:] "That's exactly it!  This is nice for many reasons, and much better than our last jump.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings are really useful to us.

Oh, rights.  Many lands be'd assert on thosun's.  A fusilly, she's a weapon, shoots a shot at high speeds usin' bang.  A mobbing, he's a grand box o' metal, pushed by burnin' and boomin' from wit'in, kennit?"

[TRANSLATE:] "Oh, yeah.  Lots of places have different words for those.  A fusilly is a weapon that fires a bullet at high speeds using propellant.  A mobbing is a big metal box that's moved around by an internal explosion.  Do you get it?

Right so, us'n'll write it in the dicky.  Here, a shiny brass farthing for crossin' the nation."

[TRANSLATE:] "Great, I'll put that in the dictionary.  Here's a token of my gratitude for your explanation.

Them's an otherlander from thrice jumps an' change, wide as the sky.  They's got happily on sommat for the tracking, you ken?"

[TRANSLATE:] "They're an otherlander from around three jumps ago, a real optimistic greenhorn.  They're really interested in how we do tracking, you see?

Hmm.  They… planned out the last jump?  Like as an apprentice to the ol' sexten."

[TRANSLATE:] "Hmm.  They… planned out the last jump?  Like an apprentice to the old tracker.

Sure an' that's a fine enough word, an I'm ken."

[TRANSLATE:] "Sure, that word is fine, I think.

Yeah, you could call us as it.  Us're from otherlands mostlike.  Not otherworlds though.  Too risky bringin' them squelchies into the fold."

[TRANSLATE:] "Yeah, you could say that.  We're from otherlands, most of the time.  Not otherworlds though.  Too risky bringing those monsters into our safe haven.

Sure an that's a biggun'.  Otherworlds be the wherefore o' them uggo buggers you got round and here, eh?  Walkin' plants and talkin' mushrooms and whatlike.  Otherlands be tassed more of a kinship.  I be from Earth, but my Earth be differed.  So you's shouldno be asked what the Exodii is doin' on Earth, because some is feelin' of us fine an' fine at home, an I'm ken.  You's should be askin' what the Exodii is doin' razzin up your green and brown."

[TRANSLATE:] "Yeah, that's a big question.  Otherworlds are how you got those ugly bug-creatures around here, you know?  Walking plants, talking mushroom, stuff like that.  Otherlands are closer related.  I'm from Earth, just a different Earth.  You shouldn't be asking what the Exodii are doing in Earth, because some of us are feeling pretty at home here, I think.  You should be asking what we're doing hanging out in your part of town.

*becomes distant for a moment.*  "Ah.  Home.  It were a long time gone, kennit.  Your'n be not too far.  I… don't think I want to talk 'bout it.  Too much metal atwixt now an' then."

[TRANSLATE:] "Ah.  Home.  That's a long time gone, you know?  Yours isn't too different.  I… don't think I want to talk about it.  I've changed too much between then and now.

Us'n saw this were a pidgeon's road, I'd razz.  Only one way, I'm ken, if I'm not to join the rank an' file."

[TRANSLATE:] "I realized that it was a no-brainer question.  There was only one other option, you see, if I didn't join the Exodii.

Robot?  What assert is f'r it?  Ahold…"  Rubik stops for a moment, as if thinking.  "Ah, an automate?  No, this'n be flesh 'n blood as ye be, encased in a shell o' metal an' wire.  Not so much flesh as there were.  The wire is amixed an' afloat with the flesh, all as one, kennit."

[TRANSLATE:] "Robot?  What does that word mean?  Hang on.  …Ah, an automate?  No, I'm as flesh and blood as you are, encased in a shell of metal and wire.  Not as much flesh as there used to be.  The wire is mixed and woven into the flesh, all as one, you see.

Yeah, that be the soggy leaves, an I'm ken.  A bit o' both, but Rubik were once as a kin, to you be."

[TRANSLATE:] "Yeah, that's the basic explanation.  A bit of both now, but I used to be just like you.

A junker base, innit?  Pile o' gamp.  Us'll pack it up and sing along soon enough."

[TRANSLATE:] "A junker base, obviously.  A jury-rigged mess.  We'll pack it up and leave eventually.

For an' how, ye be needin' to think wi' them elevens o' directions, kennit?  Us'll open a gate an' wibble-an-wobble.  Same as us came."

[TRANSLATE:] "To understand how, you've gotta think eleven-dimensionally.  We'll open up a gate and teleport out, the same as we came.

Sure as ye can, at least sommat.  Us'n'll try as we might to parley your Anglic, but so ye kennit as us be from otherlands and all, it ain't that simple."

[TRANSLATE:] "Sure you can, at least a bit.  I'll do my best to speak your Anglic, but seeing as we're from otherlands and all, it's not that simple.

Oh yeah, right and so.  Each and every.  We wander, we make do.  It's a livin'."

[TRANSLATE:] "Oh yeah, just that.  Every one of us.  We wander, we make do.  It's a living.

Same as you will be, an I'm ken.  The enemy.  The dead."

[TRANSLATE:] "Same as you, as far as I can see.  The enemy.  The dead.
Just so, aye.  Again an' again, this'n has seen it.  Too many times.

F'r to wax religious, eh?

*Rubik pauses for a while.  When they start talking again, their voice is slow and more serious than usual.*

This'n can't tell ye, rightly, but those what have a bottle an' a cork what fits it, they yark about the Enemy.  Most folks got a story like that in their ol' hearth-tales, an I'm ken.  A bad way, from times old, come back.  Ol' Rubik don't know much about that, but something makes them bodies walk and moan, and it don't seem to be somethin' of the way o' our kin.  How it gets in, well, that be anyone's for a guess.  It can come the way we came, wibbling and wobbling, but it don't always.  How it be'd the end for your deadland, Rubik can't say for ye."

[TRANSLATE:] "You want to get religious, eh?  I can't tell you for sure, but the people who claim to know, they talk about the Enemy.  Most folks have a fairy tale like that, I think.  A monster from ancient memory, returned.  I don't know much about that, but something makes those bodies walk and moan, and it doesn't seem to be anything human.  How it gets in, well, that's anyone's guess.  It can come the way we came, through a portal, but it doesn't always.  How it was for your world, I can't tell you.

No!  Bluster an' clouds, no!  *Rubik's voice comes haltingly, as if they are picking their words with unusual care for clarity.*  We done a few things what Rubik don't like to pickle an'… to think about, but never that!  We came after the fall, long after.  Always.

This be a deadland, kennit.  Spend a farthing at the pastor's house, d'ye razz?  What be left for ye?  The dead'll be in the fields, the forests, all around the green and brown.  Anything what walks, they'll salt 'n fallow, and most'll rise up and rejoin.  Those what don't, the Enemy twists and turns as well.  Every deadland be the same.  Ye've turns and twain, but come as it may, this land be dead.  Though, an I'm ken, ye've quite a few turns and twain to go yet."

[TRANSLATE:] "This is a deadland, you see.  Take a moment and look around, know what I mean?  What's left for you?  The dead will be in the fields, the forests, all over the world.  Anything that walks, they'll make it so it doesn't, and most will come back as undead.  Those that don't, the Enemy will change them as well.  Every deadland is the same.  You've years and more to go, but one way or another, this place is dead.  Though, as far as I can see, you've got quite a few years to go yet.

Spread, aye, through the wibbles, but we ain't ken on how.  After the green an' brown be to grey and black, so t'speak, Rubik be long gone.  On a moment, we folk've sent back a lover's robe or so t'the deadlands what left, but narry have returned.  An I'm ken, there be only one course from here."

[TRANSLATE:] "Spread, yes, through the portals, but we don't know how.  After the world is down to dust, I'm long gone.  Once or twice we've send back a probe to the deadlands we left behind, but none have returned.  As far as I know, there's only one way it goes from here.

If ye be champed t'try, this'n won't stop ye.  Right so, Rubik'll sell ye the pieces ye might use t'do."

[TRANSLATE:] "If you want to try it, I won't stop you.  In fact, I'll sell you equipment that might help.

Fine an' fine.  Rubik'll clarion for ye when ye stand o'er the garried trick o' Anubine hisself."

[TRANSLATE:] "You do that then.  I'll cheer for you when you stand over the vanquished corpse of the devil himself.

Makin' do, makin' do, same as you, an I'm ken.  Last home got a bit too dead 'n putrid roun' the edges, like.  Happens to the best of 'em.  Caught a jibber that made us ken 'bout your place here, fired up the ol' wibble-wammles and boom!  Now it's all tick-tock on a zimmer, here we be.  Got a good timing this time, I razz you only been dead a few days when we wobbled in.  Freshest corpse this'n's seen in a kitchen sink."

[TRANSLATE:] "Making do, making do, same as you I'd imagine.  Our last home got too dead and putrid around the edges, basically.  It happens to the best of them.  We caught some news that brought us along to your place here, fired up the engines, and boom!  Now, quick as can be, here we are.  We got a good timing this time, seems to me you'd only been dead a few days when we got here.  Freshest corpse I've seen in a while.

Us're here to live and breathe, kennit?  After our last otherland got a li'l too dead an' all.  So, us'n came to a new place.  This'n.  An I'm ken, it's not so long dead round here jus' yet."

[TRANSLATE:] "English: We're just here to survive, you understand?  Our last world got too overrun with undead.  So, we came to a new world.  This one.  If I'm not mistaken, it's not so long dead around here just yet.

Aside from jus' livin' in such a cozy nook?  Us be minin', ye kennit.  Pickin' the scraps, seein' if for your otherland has any tech worth an upside-down.  No sense lettin' good scraps go to waste.  If we’re lucky, pickin' a few new Exodii afore we wobble out.  Pickin' up the pieces of our sweet, shattered dreams, suchlike."

[TRANSLATE:] "English: Aside from just having a safe place to live?  We're here to mine, you understand.  Picking the scraps, seeing if this world has any tech worth reverse engineering.  No sense letting good scraps go to waste.  If we're lucky, maybe we'll get some new Exodii before we teleport out.  Pickin' up the pieces of our sweet, shattered dreams, such as they are.

This'n be a deadland, an I'm ken.  You gots you a case o' the willies ain't gonna sing along.  No cure for these rats and fleas."

[TRANSLATE:] "English: This is a deadland, don't you see?  You've already got an infestation and it's not going away.  There's no cure for the zombies.

Means what it means.  Your land's a deadun', still kickin' is all."

[TRANSLATE:] "English: It means what it means.  Your land's dead already, it's just still kicking is all.

Oh, us can wobble along as needs.  Sends the scrap back, brings in the foods, and shakes off a willie or three, kennit.  No good for you, won’t take too much meat-an'-bone."

[TRANSLATE:] "English: Oh, we can teleport along as we need to.  We send the scrap along, then the food, and shake off some baddies, you understand.  It's no good for you though, it won't take too much flesh and bone.

Haha, not mostly, mate.  Not worth riskin’ the willies, innit?  I keep what's Rubik, but the rest is all solid."

[TRANSLATE:] "Haha, not mostly, mate.  It's not worth risking the side effects, you see?  I keep the parts of me that make me Rubik, but the rest is all solid.

Oh, sure an it's bagged in a coffer an' all that.  That is t'say, this'n does get a wipe o' a grinny t'see the perplexion upon a visage, an I'm ken.*  You're pretty sure you hear a faint chuckle in the metallic voice.  *What I be meanin' is at, for my body were t'be meat-an'-bone, the tool what we be usin' for t'travel to an' fro, it rips up the meat an' leaves it a right mess.  A bit can come along for a right fun, but too much… on a time, an earlier Rubik felt a spot o' those willies, an' this'n be not in the farrier's hut for t'try it again."

[TRANSLATE:] "Oh, sure, that's a fair assessment.  I mean, I do get a bit of a laugh out of the look on your face sometimes.  What I'm saying is, if my body were flesh and bone, the device we use to travel around dimensions would rip up the meat and leave me quite a mess.  We can take a bit, but too much… once time, I felt a bit of that, and I'm not in any rush to try it again.

Not to me it don't.  We ain't tassed from around here though.  Looks fine an' fine to you I'd razz."

[TRANSLATE:] "Not to me it doesn't.  We didn't get it from around here though.  I bet it looks pretty nice to you.

If'n you're full an' plenty, this'n's happy to make the call, for a shiny farthing."

[TRANSLATE:] "If you've got what I need, I'm happy to call ahead and make the arrangements, for a fee.

data.dynamic_line:
THIS'n's accent?  Ye've never egged y'r own yark, an' that's a fine fiddle.  Great Grey has a bit o' work on it, kennit?  This'n has to keep usselves useful, an' keep Great Grey doin' what it's tassed.  Asides, yarkin' to the local brights keeps us young an' shines our chrome, an I'm ken."

[TRANSLATE:] "MY accent?  You've obviously never had to listen to yourself talk.  Great Grey has more important work to do, get it?  I have to keep myself useful and keep Gret Grey doing what it's supposed to.  Besides, talking to the locals keeps me young and shines my chrome, as I see it.

Fine an' fine, an' fine an' fine!  Ha!  Us'll rubber up the ol' gristle mill.  Yer tassed wi' bringin' us a nip o' good tea.  Not 'tea', o'course.  I'm yarkin dockside Anglic here.  Us means the stuff what puts y'to sleep f'r a chirurgery.  The Great Grey says y'r assert for it is 'anus fetick'.  You bring us a thousand unit of 'anus fetick', us'll fix'n ye up with a wire an' a tiff."

[TRANSLATE:] "Great, great, great!!  Ha!  We'll fire up the old meat grinder.  Your job is to bring us a bit of good tea.  Not literally 'tea' of course.  That's my Anglic street slang.  I mean the stuff that puts you to sleep for surgery.  The Great Grey says your word for it is 'anesthetic'.  You bring us a thousand units of anesthetic, we'll fix you up with a wire and everything.

[TRANSLATE:] "Great, great, great!!  Ha!  We'll fire up the old meat grinder.  You just come along with old Rubik.

[TRANSLATE:] "That's a fine choice, I understand.  If you change your mind, old Rubik's going to be here for a while.  You'll get to know us better, we'll get to know you better, and that's going to be good all around.
